column15: Confirmed real own-label blended Scotch (not the bank) by Campbell Meyer & Company Ltd, East Kilbride, Scotland -- verified on their own product page, which also states peatProfile=light ("a trace of peat smoke, suggesting some Islay malt has been used", "hint of smoke in the finish"), satisfying producer-domain corroboration for the positive peat claim.

Corrected: real blended Irish whiskey, core release of Lough Ree Distillery (Lanesborough, Co. Longford) sold ahead of their own single malt maturing -- new row lough-ree added, parentSlug set. A search summary described the blend as including "peated malt" among grain/pot-still components, but Whisky Magazine's tasting notes (opened this session) show no smoky/peaty character at all, so peatProfile kept unknown rather than asserted; withheld peat proposal: possibly light if the peated-malt component is confirmed material, per an unopened secondary source.

Corrected kind to brand (spans single malt and blended releases, not one blend recipe). Confirmed via the producer's own domain: made by Maison Daucourt, a French spirits house ("four generations of Charente expertise"), founded by Edouard Daucourt in 2010, produced entirely in France -- new row maison-daucourt added (also makes D.U.C, see d-u-c row), parentSlug set. No peat/smoke mentioned. The seed's note that "Daucourt" was "only a French surname, not a spirits company" was wrong -- Maison Daucourt is exactly the company behind this brand.

Corrected kind from blend to distillery: Beara Distillery Ltd, Castletownbere Commercial Park, Co. Cork, Ireland. Makes single malt, single grain AND the Black Cask Blend (matches both catalogue samples exactly), so defaultTypeName left empty (multi-type range). No peat/smoke mentioned in the official description (toasted oak, malt, fruit, spice notes only).

Corrected: countryCode filled FR (was empty) and kind confirmed distillery -- produced by Les Bienheureux SAS, St Andre de Cubzac, France, who distil in Charentais pot stills and column stills ("reindustrializing French whiskey production"). Also makes a "Pur Malt" (single malt) expression besides Triple Grain, so defaultTypeName left empty rather than "grain". A secondary source (not opened this session) described Triple Grain as "not peated", but the whisky.fr product page itself (opened) makes no peat/smoke statement, so peatProfile kept unknown rather than asserted as none.

Corrected kind to brand: Bell Rock American Whiskey is one of several brands (also Cumberland Falls Bourbon, plus vodka/gin/rum/tequila) owned by Global Spirits, a large European alcohol holding (Khortytsa Distillery, Odessa Cognac Factory); the liquid itself is made at a family-owned distillery in Florida. Four flavored/plain expressions (American Whiskey, Apple & Honey, Butterscotch Bourbon, Cinnamon), so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Confirmed: Boone County Distilling Co., Independence, Boone County, Kentucky ("Born in 1833 - Reborn in 2015") -- verified via the distillery's own site (previously only assumed from general knowledge). Its homepage describes itself as making Kentucky bourbon; a third-party site additionally claims a rye line, so defaultTypeName is left empty rather than asserting bourbon uniformly. peatProfile=none rests on the well-established bourbon-category fact (no peat-smoking step in bourbon production), confirmed by re-reading the Wikipedia bourbon article this session, not on a brand-specific statement.

Re-verified this session (was already high-quality in the seed): 100% organic, seed-to-spirit French single malt distilled in Cognac, founded by Allison Parc, now owned by Local Infusions LLC (a Samson & Surrey company). No peat/smoke mentioned; confidence raised from low to high since the identity/facts are directly confirmed on the producer's own domain.

Corrected: real German whisky, a licensed collaboration with actor Bud Spencer, produced by St. Kilian Distillers, Ruedenau, Germany -- new row st-kilian added, parentSlug set, countryCode corrected to DE (was XX). This batch's un-suffixed samples ("The Legend", "The Legend Mini") match St Kilian's "Legend Mild Blended Malt" expression, explicitly described by a retailer as harmonizing "the non-peated blend of grains" -- peatProfile=none. St Kilian separately also sells a smoky "Legend Rauchig Single Malt" and a stand-alone "St. Kilian PEATED" bottling; flagging for reviewer in case the 0.05L "Mini" ever turns out to be a mini of the Rauchig line rather than of the Mild one. defaultTypeName left empty since the brand's range spans both "blended malt" (Mild) and "single malt" (Rauchig) labels.

Corrected bottlerSlug: removed (was cadenhead) -- maltfascination.com (opened) confirms "Burnside" is a shared teaspoon pseudonym for Balvenie (with a touch of Glenfiddich) used by AT LEAST five different independent bottlers (Cadenhead's, Whisky Center, Archives, Berry Bros & Rudd, C. Dully Selection), not Cadenhead exclusively -- this batch's own second sample ("Scyfion Burnside 1999") independently confirms a sixth bottler, Scyfion, also uses it. parentSlug=balvenie kept (solidly confirmed). Corrected kind to blend and defaultTypeName from "single malt" to "malt": teaspooning legally requires the "blended malt" declaration, it is never sold as single malt. peatProfile=none reflects Balvenie's famously unpeated standard range; flag for reviewer: Balvenie has released occasional official "Peated Cask"/"Triple Cask...Peated" special editions per Wikipedia, so this is a house-style default rather than a guarantee no Burnside cask ever drew on peated stock -- no evidence found that any did.

Major correction: this is a PEATED blended malt range, produced by Torabhaig Distillery (Skye) itself, owned by Mossburn Distillers -- confirmed directly on torabhaig.com, whose collection page describes the whole range as peated and smoky with a rugged Hebridean character, and whose entry-level bottling page states "heavy Island peat notes". parentSlug=torabhaig added (Torabhaig is already a live KB row) alongside owner=Mossburn Distillers. region=islands/legalRegion=highland per the market-vs-legal Skye pattern (same as Talisker/Highland Park/Tobermory/Jura/Arran). defaultTypeName=malt (all three listed expressions -- standard, 12yo, 15yo -- are "Blended Malt Scotch Whisky"). A further-elevated "12 Year Old Heavily Peated Oloroso Finish" line extension also exists; if the catalogue ever carries it as a distinctly named product it should get its own row rather than share this one.

Corrected: this is an independently-bottled single malt Scotch brand (NAS, 12 Year Old, and limited single-cask releases from named distilleries such as Ardmore and Bunnahabhain) from Charles Edge London, an independent bottler -- new row charles-edge added (kind=bottler), bottlerSlug set. The name does reference the historic King Malcolm III "Canmore" line as the seed guessed. defaultTypeName=single malt (every known expression is single malt). peatProfile kept unknown: single-cask sources vary (e.g. Ardmore is lightly peated Highland, Bunnahabhain's core range is unpeated), so no uniform level can be asserted for the brand.

Confirmed via the distillery's own site (was previously unresearched, working from general knowledge only): Catoctin Creek Distilling Company, Purcellville, Loudoun County, Virginia, founded 2009, "The Virginia Rye Whisky", Roundstone Rye flagship -- matches both catalogue samples. defaultTypeName=rye confirmed (their whisky range, as opposed to gin/brandy, is rye-only). No peat/smoke mentioned on the official site; kept unknown rather than asserting none since American rye whiskey has no blanket no-peat guarantee as strong as bourbon's.

Major correction: "Mallows" is NOT a marshmallow-flavor descriptor -- it is Mallows Beverages, a real Welsh spirits company, and "Charlie Parry's" is "the first Welsh bourbon" (born in America, aged/finished in Wales). countryCode corrected to GB-WLS (was US); owner=Mallows Beverages added. The range spans straight bourbon (3 Year Old, Blended) and flavored bourbon liqueurs (honey, coffee, chocolate, cinnamon, apple, berry), so defaultTypeName left empty. peatProfile=none per the bourbon-style category default; no peat/smoke mentioned.

Corrected: real "well spirits" (bar-pour) brand spanning whiskey, rum, gin, vodka, tequila and scotch, confirmed via the producer's own site -- "Bottled by American Distilling Co., Mira Loma, CA" -- new row american-distilling-co added (kind=bottler), bottlerSlug set. Whiskey line alone spans Cinnamon Whiskey, Blended Scotch, Blended Whiskey and Bourbon sub-labels, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned.

Resolved the seed's open question: Corsair's own shop page confirms Triple Smoke uses THREE individually smoked malts -- cherrywood (Wisconsin), beechwood (Germany), AND peat (Scotland) -- satisfying the producer-domain requirement for a positive claim. Since peat is only one of three smoke sources (diluted, not straight peated malt), set to light rather than medium/heavy. Nashville, TN craft distillery; range still spans single malt and rye (e.g. Dark Rye sample), so defaultTypeName stays empty. Misspelling "Corsaire" already captured in the row's existing aliases.

Corrected: this is a real French whisky, "the result of a double distillation and aging in two types of casks" (Double Cask / Triple Cask), made from malted barley, wheat and corn in a Charentais pot still -- countryCode corrected to FR (was XX). Produced by Maison Daucourt, the SAME company behind Bastille 1789 (see bastille row) -- confirmed independently on both daucourt.com and ducwhisky.com; parentSlug=maison-daucourt set (new row). No peat/smoke mentioned. defaultTypeName left empty: the malted-barley/wheat/corn mash bill does not map cleanly onto the closed single malt/grain vocabulary.

Confirmed current producer (the seed could not find one): Lux Row Distillers, Bardstown, Kentucky -- new row lux-row-distillers added, bottlerSlug set. Historic recipe: David Nicholson created the "43" bourbon recipe in his St. Louis grocery store around 1843, later produced at the A. Ph. Stitzel distillery (Van Winkle family), now at Lux Row. Both catalogue samples confirmed as named expressions: "1843" (wheated bourbon) and "Reserve" (ryed/extra-aged bourbon) -- both legally bourbon, so defaultTypeName=bourbon. The site's "woody and smoky tones" tasting note is oak-char derived, not peat; peatProfile=none per the bourbon-category default, no peat mentioned.

Confirmed producer (the seed could not find one): Walsh Whiskey, the independent Irish company founded by Bernard and Rosemary Walsh (also behind the already-live Writers' Tears and The Irishman) -- confirmed via a retailer product page naming Walsh Whiskey as producer, and via walshwhiskey.com directly (though De Danann is not listed among their CURRENT homepage brands, suggesting an older or export-market line). owner=Walsh Whiskey added. Sample "De Danann Walsh" corroborates the link. No smoke/peat in either the walshwhiskey.com general content or the retailer's tasting notes for this specific blend, so peatProfile=none.

Confirmed via the distillery's own site (previously the seed could only infer the location from an area code): FEW Spirits, Evanston, Illinois, founded 2011, grain-to-glass, makes bourbon and rye ("a bold Chicago-style twist"). Dropped the seed's irrelevant Irish-whiskey Wikipedia citation. defaultTypeName left empty since the range is bourbon AND rye, not one type. peatProfile=none per the craft American bourbon/rye category default; no peat/smoke mentioned on site.

Resolved the seed's reviewer flag: Whisky Advocate (opened this session) confirms the Sheep Dung Smoked Reserve uses no peat at all -- the malt is dried over smoke from burning dried sheep dung, a traditional Icelandic method, rather than a peat fire. This is genuine non-peat smokiness; see the companion rule.tsv entry (flavor=smoky, effect=require) for that specific expression. peatProfile=none set at the producer level since no Floki expression is peat-smoked. countryCode stays XX: Iceland has no code in the closed list. The distillery's own domain (flokiwhisky.is) was unreachable both by the seed and by this session (504/timeout); relying on Whisky Advocate plus multiple independent retailer/press mentions of Eimverk Distillery, Iceland's only whisky distillery, founded 2009.

Researched (seed budget had skipped it): Fordman Kentucky Straight Bourbon is an export-market bourbon brand owned by La Martiniquaise (a French spirits group), with the liquid outsourced to Heaven Hill's Bernheim Distillery in Kentucky -- bottlerSlug=heaven-hill set (already a live KB row); owner=La Martiniquaise added. Confirmed mash bill (51% corn / 49% other grains, double distilled, 2+ years in new charred oak) legally qualifies as bourbon, matching the sole catalogue sample. peatProfile=none per the bourbon-category default.

New row for bastille and d-u-c: French spirits house ("spirit producers for four generations"), Charentais pot-still double distillation, based in the St Andre de Cubzac / Charente area. Confirmed on daucourt.com's own product listing to produce BOTH D.U.C Whisky and BASTILLE Whisky 1789, plus Moulin Vodka, Or-G Liqueur and New Angouleme Gin. No peat/smoke mentioned on any of the three official domains checked (daucourt.com, ducwhisky.com, bastillewhisky.com).

New row for bud-spencer: German single malt whisky distillery, Ruedenau (Hauptstrasse 1-5, 63924), founded 2012 ("reines Gerstenmalz trifft bei uns auf Kupferbrennblasen" -- pure barley malt meets our copper pot stills). Runs licensed collaboration lines (Bud Spencer & Terence Hill, Scorpions Rock Editions) alongside its own-name single malt range, plus gin and liqueurs. Per third-party retailers (not this domain), the distillery also bottles at least one product literally named "St. Kilian PEATED" and a smoky "Rauchig" line, so it does produce genuinely peated single malt among its own releases -- peatProfile left unknown at the distillery-row level since its range spans both peated and unpeated; judge per specific expression.

New row for barts: family-owned microdistillery in Lanesborough, Co. Longford, on the River Shannon/Lough Ree. Distilling gin & vodka since 2018, Irish whiskey since 2022 (Ireland's smallest GI-verified Irish whiskey distillery). Bart's blended Irish whiskey is its core release, sold ahead of its own single malt ("The Bridge") maturing. No peat/smoke statement found for the distillery generally.

New row for canmore: independent bottler and blender of Scotch whisky, "Charles Edge London"; also runs the London Square (gin) and Scots Gold brands. countryCode set to GB-ENG for the company's own registered base (London); its whisky output is entirely Scotch sourced from Scottish distilleries -- flag for reviewer if the KB's convention for Scotch-only English bottlers differs (e.g. codes such companies GB-SCT instead, matching the product rather than the office).

New row for david-nicholson: Bardstown, Kentucky bourbon distillery (address "1 Lux Row, Bardstown, KY 40004"), current home of the David Nicholson brand. peatProfile=none per the general Kentucky-bourbon category fact; no peat mentioned on site.

New row for conciere: bottling company named on Conciere's own product page ("Bottled by American Distilling Co., Mira Loma, CA"), a well/value-spirits line spanning whiskey, rum, gin, vodka, tequila. No further detail confirmed this session beyond the bottling credit.
